## ecfr-20-cfr-639-3-employer

- **Source:** 20 CFR 639.3(a): WARN definition of employer, National Archives, Electronic Code of Federal Regulations
- **URL:** https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-V/part-639/section-639.3
- **Supports:** WARN applies to employers with 100 or more employees excluding part-time workers, or 100 or more including part-time workers who together work at least 4,000 hours a week.
- **Quote:** "(i) 100 or more employees, excluding part-time employees; or (ii) 100 or more employees, including part-time employees, who in the aggregate work at least 4,000 hours per week, exclusive of hours of overtime."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-11-26

## ecfr-20-cfr-639-4-60-day-notice

- **Source:** 20 CFR 639.4: WARN 60-day notice, National Archives, Electronic Code of Federal Regulations
- **URL:** https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-V/part-639/section-639.4
- **Supports:** A WARN-covered employer must give 60 days' written notice before a plant closing or mass layoff.
- **Quote:** "Section 3(a) of WARN states that “an employer shall not order a plant closing or mass layoff until the end of a 60-day period after the employer serves written notice of such an order * * *.”"
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-11-26

## ecfr-20-cfr-639-4-sale-of-business

- **Source:** 20 CFR 639.4(c): WARN notice in the sale of a business, National Archives, Electronic Code of Federal Regulations
- **URL:** https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-V/part-639/section-639.4
- **Supports:** Under the WARN regulations the seller gives notice for closings or mass layoffs up to the sale date, and the buyer for those after it.
- **Quote:** "The seller is responsible for providing notice of any plant closing or mass layoff which takes place up to and including the effective date (time) of the sale, and the buyer is responsible for providing notice of any plant closing or mass layoff that takes place thereafter."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-11-26

## irs-pub-15-successor-ein

- **Source:** Publication 15 (Circular E), Employer’s Tax Guide: EIN after taking over a business, Internal Revenue Service
- **URL:** https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15
- **Supports:** A buyer that takes over another employer's business does not use the seller's employer identification number.
- **Quote:** "If you took over another employer’s business (see Successor employer in section 9), don’t use that employer’s EIN."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## irs-pub-15-successor-w4

- **Source:** Publication 15 (Circular E): Forms W-4 from transferred employees, Internal Revenue Service
- **URL:** https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15
- **Supports:** A successor employer gets new Forms W-4 from transferred employees unless the alternative procedure in Rev. Proc. 2004-53 applies.
- **Quote:** "If you’re a successor employer (see Successor employer, later in this section), secure new Forms W-4 from the transferred employees unless the “Alternative Procedure” in section 5 of Revenue Procedure 2004-53 applies."

## irs-worker-classification

- **Source:** Independent contractor (self-employed) or employee?, Internal Revenue Service
- **URL:** https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/independent-contractor-self-employed-or-employee
- **Supports:** The IRS weighs behavioral control, financial control and the type of relationship to decide whether a worker is an employee or a contractor.
- **Quote:** "Facts that provide evidence of the degree of control and independence fall into three categories: Behavioral: Does the company control or have the right to control what the worker does and how the worker does his or her job? ## uscis-i9-section-2-timing

- **Source:** Completing Section 2: Employer Review and Attestation, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services
- **URL:** https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/complete-correct-form-i-9/completing-section-2-employer-review-and-attestation
- **Supports:** Section 2 of Form I-9 must be completed within 3 business days of an employee's first day of work for pay.

## uscis-m274-acquisitions

- **Source:** Handbook for Employers M-274, 8.0: acquisitions and mergers, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services
- **URL:** https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/form-i-9-resources/handbook-for-employers-m-274/80-rules-for-continuing-employment-and-other-special-rules
- **Supports:** An employer that acquires or merges with a company has two options for Forms I-9; the first is to treat acquired employees as new hires and complete new forms for all of them.
- **Quote:** "Employers who have acquired or merged with another company have two options: Option A: Treat all acquired employees as new hires and complete a new Form I-9 for every individual."

## uscis-m274-acquisitions-option-b

- **Source:** Handbook for Employers M-274, 8.0: keeping the previous owner’s Forms I-9, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services
- **URL:** https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/form-i-9-resources/handbook-for-employers-m-274/80-rules-for-continuing-employment-and-other-special-rules
- **Supports:** A buyer that keeps the previous owner's Forms I-9 is liable for any errors or omissions on them.
- **Quote:** "Option B: Treat all acquired individuals as employees who are continuing in their uninterrupted employment status and retain the previous owner’s Form I-9 for each acquired employee. You will be liable for any errors or omissions on the previously completed Form I-9."
